01-ilo.title: ILO: secure and fast, but no entity markup.
01-ilo.linkedin:
ILO: secure and fast, but no entity markup.

security.txt is published, HSTS covers subdomains, and DMARC rejects spoofed mail. But no page read carries JSON-LD, so the Facebook, LinkedIn and YouTube profiles it links are never tied to the ILO.

The lesson for every team: Add Organization markup with url, logo and sameAs so AI answers name you right.

One automated read of public pages on 21 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict.

02-policiaco.title: Policía Nacional's search has no label.
02-policiaco.linkedin:
Policía Nacional's search has no label.

HSTS with preload, framing limited to its own origin, a declared language, and every internal link opened answered. But the home page search box and volume slider have no label, so screen readers announce blank fields.

The lesson for every team: Tie each field to a <label for>, or give it an aria-label. A screen reader can only announce a name that exists.

One automated read of public pages on 21 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict.
How the review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=runs-3-2027-03&utm_content=policiaco

03-valle.title: Valle del Cauca locks the pinch-zoom.
03-valle.linkedin:
Valle del Cauca locks the pinch-zoom.

HSTS runs a full year, framing is limited, and cookies are Secure. But the viewport tag says user-scalable=no, so people who need larger text cannot pinch to zoom on a phone.

The lesson for every team: Drop user-scalable=no and maximum-scale from the viewport tag, so people can zoom to at least 200%.

The lesson for every team: Wrap each page's content in one <main>, which screen readers offer as a skip link.

05-wto.title: WTO: no viewport tag on the start page.
05-wto.linkedin:
WTO: no viewport tag on the start page.

HSTS is on, framing is limited to the same origin, and DMARC rejects spoofed mail. But the start page has no viewport meta tag, so phones draw the desktop layout zoomed out, and Google indexes mobile first.

The lesson for every team: Add a viewport meta tag with width=device-width, initial-scale=1, then test on a phone.

One automated read of public pages on 21 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict.

06-gobmx.title: Gob.mx can be framed by any other site.
06-gobmx.linkedin:
Gob.mx can be framed by any other site.

A permanent https redirect, real 404s for unknown paths, and pages that read well without JavaScript. But the start page sends no X-Frame-Options, no CSP frame-ancestors, and no HSTS, so any site can load it in a frame.

The lesson for every team: Send frame-ancestors 'self' in a CSP, or X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN. It stops clickjacking on forms.

One automated read of public pages on 21 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict.
How the review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=runs-3-2027-03&utm_content=gobmx

09-wmo.title: WMO's sitemap points at other hosts.
09-wmo.linkedin:
WMO's sitemap points at other hosts.

HSTS is sent with preload, every image read has alt text, and language versions link back to each other. But the sitemap lists 878 community.wmo.int URLs, and search engines skip sitemap URLs from another host.

The lesson for every team: Keep each sitemap to its own host. Give each subdomain its own sitemap, named in that subdomain's robots.txt.

The lesson for every team: Set security headers at the edge, not per app, so every path on the host gets the same HSTS policy.
